bibl.title: Estimating the population abundance of tissue-infiltrating immune and stromal cell populations using gene expression

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how much of each immune and stromal cell population is present in a tissue sample, read out of a bulk transcriptome - and what kind of comparison the resulting number licenses
span.quote: We introduce the Microenvironment Cell Populations-counter (MCP-counter) method, which allows the robust quantification of the absolute abundance of eight immune and two stromal cell populations in heterogeneous tissues from transcriptomic data. We present in vitro mRNA mixture and ex vivo immunohistochemical data that quantitatively support the validity of our method’s estimates.

span.label: whether markers exist that are expressed in one and only one cell population, and whether their average expression tracks that population's abundance well enough to compare samples
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: MCP-counter - ten populations scored from data-driven transcriptomic markers selected against curated negative controls, validated against in vitro RNA mixtures and against immunohistochemical cell densities, and explicitly scoped to inter-sample comparison in arbitrary units
span.quote: We introduce the Microenvironment Cell Populations-counter (MCP-counter) method, which allows the robust quantification of the absolute abundance of eight immune and two stromal cell populations in heterogeneous tissues from transcriptomic data. We present in vitro mRNA mixture and ex vivo immunohistochemical data that quantitatively support the validity of our method’s estimates.

span.label: method
span.quote: We introduce the Microenvironment Cell Populations-counter (MCP-counter) method, which allows the robust quantification of the absolute abundance of eight immune and two stromal cell populations in heterogeneous tissues from transcriptomic data. We present in vitro mRNA mixture and ex vivo immunohistochemical data that quantitatively support the validity of our method’s estimates.

span.label: a bulk transcriptome averaging signals from every cell type present, so that the composition of the tissue is recoverable only through markers that belong to one population and nothing else
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: markers selected on three simultaneous thresholds against 1194 purified microenvironment samples and 742 tumour cell lines as negative controls, scored as the log2 mean of their expression, validated on 4804 further samples, on latin-square RNA mixtures and on 38 immunohistochemically quantified tumours
span.term: markers selected on three simultaneous thresholds against 1194 purified microenvironment samples and 742 tumour cell lines as negative controls, scored as the log2 mean of their expression, validated on 4804 further samples, on latin-square RNA mixtures and on 38 immunohistochemically quantified tumours
span.quote: These transcriptomes were normalized to allow their integration into a large meta-dataset which includes 1194 immune or non-immune microenvironment cell population samples; 742 tumor cell line samples were included as negative controls (Additional file 1: Table S1). No hematopoietic tumor cell line was included as a negative control as the transcriptome of these cells is closely related to that of non-malignant hematopoietic cells.

span.label: if a gene is expressed in exactly one cell type and at a stable level within it, then its expression in a mixture is proportional to how much of that cell type is there - no unmixing, no reference matrix, no dependence on what else is in the sample. The whole method is that one property, and the paper says such genes are not guaranteed to exist
span.term: a marker that belongs to one population and nothing else
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: a marker qualifies by separating positive from negative samples, so a population with no purified counter-example in a public repository cannot be given markers at all. Effector memory CD4 T cells are named as a casualty: they would need central memory CD4 and effector memory CD8 controls, and those were not available
span.quote: We thus discarded those for which appropriate negative controls were not publically available (for instance, identifying TM for effector memory CD4 T cells at least requires negative controls such as central memory CD4 T cells and effector memory CD8 T cells), those with few positive samples, or those with no identified markers after the selection procedure.

span.label: 21 cancer types among the negative controls make the markers portable across tissues and remove any marker that any of those tissues expresses. NCAM1/CD56, a standard NK marker, is discarded because nervous malignant cells carry it - which protects every other tissue and gives up NK quantification in brain
span.quote: This large diversity of control samples may, however, discard TM which would be relevant in a specific setting: for instance, the screening procedure discarded NCAM1 (CD56), a widely used marker of NK cells, as it is also expressed by nervous malignant cells and is thus unsuitable to quantify NK cells in brain samples.

span.label: the score is a log2 mean of marker expression, so it moves with abundance and has no absolute meaning. Two consequences the paper states: the units depend on the measurement platform, and mapping them onto percentages would require calibrating samples of known composition - which is the step aran2017 later takes
span.term: a scale with no zero and no unit
span.quote: To complement the current multi-sample use of MCP-counter, designed for exploratory analyses, one could notably settle on a desired gene expression platform and use a set of calibrating samples. For instance, the in vitro RNA mixtures described here could help to map MCP-counter abundance scores to non-arbitrary units, such as the percentage of the corresponding cells within a sample. Setting-specific tuning may, however, be required to reach the reliability necessary for clinical protocols.

span.label: the scores are in arbitrary units that depend on the gene expression platform, so only samples produced on the same platform can be compared
span.quote: MCP-counter scores linearly correlate with the corresponding cell population abundances across samples, but they are expressed in arbitrary units. These arbitrary units are dependent on the gene expression platform used to produce the data and one can only compare samples produced with the same gene expression platforms.

span.label: transcriptomic markers are not guaranteed to exist for a given population, because the definition requires expression in one and only one cell type
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: populations without publicly available negative controls were dropped from the method regardless of their interest
span.quote: We thus discarded those for which appropriate negative controls were not publically available (for instance, identifying TM for effector memory CD4 T cells at least requires negative controls such as central memory CD4 T cells and effector memory CD8 T cells), those with few positive samples, or those with no identified markers after the selection procedure.

span.label: the breadth of the control set discards markers that would work in a restricted setting - NCAM1 is lost because nervous malignant cells express it
span.quote: This large diversity of control samples may, however, discard TM which would be relevant in a specific setting: for instance, the screening procedure discarded NCAM1 (CD56), a widely used marker of NK cells, as it is also expressed by nervous malignant cells and is thus unsuitable to quantify NK cells in brain samples.

span.label: spatial localisation is lost relative to immunohistochemistry, and histological confirmation may be needed where contamination by surrounding tissue is unavoidable
span.quote: Information of the cells’ spatial localization, which is available in IHC experiments, is lost, however, when using transcriptomic technologies. Histological confirmation of MCP-counter estimates may thus be necessary in cases where contamination of samples by surrounding tissues is unavoidable.

span.label: accuracy depends on the quality of the expression summary, and the populations estimated are usually rare, so high sequencing depth may be required
span.quote: Nonetheless, since MCP-counter scores are based on summarized gene expression features (such as reads per kilobase per millions), its accuracy may suffer if the quality of this summary is low. The cell populations whose abundance is estimated by MCP-counter are usually at relatively low frequencies in tissue samples. Thus, sequencing samples at high depth (>80 million reads per sample), which has been reported to improve the quantification of rare transcripts, may improve the accuracy of MCP-counter estimates from RNA-sequencing samples.

span.label: the prognostic meta-analysis is univariate and unadjusted for stage or treatment
span.quote: Although this univariate analysis was not adjusted for variables potentially influencing OS, such as tumor stage or treatments received, it nonetheless appeared consistent with the published literature, notably revealing an overall favorable prognosis associated with infiltration by T cells, except in kidney clear-cell carcinoma as previously reported and in low grade glioma.

span.label: surprising tissue-level results are referred back to histopathological knowledge rather than defended - the authors say the method should be compared against it
span.quote: Other results appeared more surprising, such as the high abundance of fibroblastic cells in the microenvironment of stromal tumors—which may originate from a subset of dedifferentiated tumor cells or the relatively low vascularization of hepatocellular carcinoma samples—which is possibly due to the unique phenotype of endothelial cells in the liver. MCP-counter should in these cases be compared with histopathological knowledge and data within a given cancer.

span.label: the cytotoxic lymphocyte population's mRNA was not controlled in the mixture experiment, so its validation is a linear model on the other populations rather than a direct calibration
span.quote: Finally, although the amount of cytotoxic lymphocyte mRNA was not controlled in our mixture experiment, we tested whether the CD3+ T cells (through their CD8+ subset) and the NK cells contributed to the level of the cytotoxic lymphocyte MCP-counter score. We thus performed a linear model (“Methods”) which revealed that both cell types contributed significantly and positively to the level of the cytotoxic lymphocyte score, jointly explaining 99 % of the observed variance (Fig. 3d; p = 1.3 × 10−9 for NK cells and p = 0.038 for CD3+ T cells, R2 = 0.99).

span.label: the latin square, carried from agricultural experimental design into the layout of an RNA mixture so that no two populations' concentrations are collinear
span.quote: For this purpose, we designed an in vitro RNA mixture experiment (Fig. 3a). Immune populations were purified from healthy donors’ peripheral blood; their RNAs were extracted and mixed in highly variable concentrations (from 0.7 to 46 % of the sample’s RNA). The RNA proportions of the populations were arranged in two transposed latin squares to avoid collinearity and thus ensure specificity (Additional file 1: Table S10). The mixtures were further diluted in a fixed amount of a solution containing mRNA extracted from HCT-116, a colorectal cancer cell line.

span.label: the ROC curve and the signal-to-noise ratio, carried from signal detection into the selection criteria for a gene marker
span.quote: Three criteria were then calculated for each feature (probe set) within the discovery set: a) the mean log2-expression difference between positive and negative samples (a threshold of 2 was applied); b) the area under the ROC curve (AUC) of the feature for the identification of the positive samples (threshold of 0.97); and c) a measure of the signal to noise ratio between positive and negative samples (threshold of 1.5) (“Methods”; Additional file 1: Table S2). Gene expression features that reached the defined thresholds simultaneously for all three criteria were retained as TM for the corresponding cell population.

span.label: 742 tumour cell line samples from 21 non-hematopoietic cancer types included as negative controls, with no hematopoietic line included and the reason stated
span.note: eliminates: a marker that is merely abundant being taken for a marker that is specific - and the exclusion of hematopoietic lines removes a control that would have looked like the positive class · outcome: held
span.quote: These transcriptomes were normalized to allow their integration into a large meta-dataset which includes 1194 immune or non-immune microenvironment cell population samples; 742 tumor cell line samples were included as negative controls (Additional file 1: Table S1). No hematopoietic tumor cell line was included as a negative control as the transcriptome of these cells is closely related to that of non-malignant hematopoietic cells.

span.label: three simultaneous thresholds per candidate feature - a log2 expression difference, an AUC for identifying positive samples, and a signal-to-noise ratio
span.note: eliminates: a feature qualifying on one favourable statistic; all three must be met at once, which is what makes the marker set conservative rather than large · outcome: held
span.quote: Three criteria were then calculated for each feature (probe set) within the discovery set: a) the mean log2-expression difference between positive and negative samples (a threshold of 2 was applied); b) the area under the ROC curve (AUC) of the feature for the identification of the positive samples (threshold of 0.97); and c) a measure of the signal to noise ratio between positive and negative samples (threshold of 1.5) (“Methods”; Additional file 1: Table S2). Gene expression features that reached the defined thresholds simultaneously for all three criteria were retained as TM for the corresponding cell population.

span.label: two independent validation series on different array platforms, 4804 samples, with the selection criteria re-applied to see whether the same markers come out
span.note: eliminates: the marker sets being an artefact of the discovery data or of one array platform - the overlap is tested for significance rather than eyeballed · outcome: held
span.quote: The reproducibility of the identified TM was assessed on two micrenvironment validation series of 1596 samples hybridized on Affymetrix U133A arrays and 3208 samples hybridized on Affymetrix HuGene 1.0ST arrays (Additional file 1: Tables S4 and 5). For the ten cell populations, the specific expression patterns obtained on the discovery series were consistently reproduced (Additional file 2: Figure S3), and the same selection criteria applied to MCP validation series identified significantly overlapping TM sets

span.label: an in vitro RNA mixture experiment with the populations laid out in two transposed latin squares
span.note: eliminates: collinearity between the populations - without the latin square, a score could track its own population or any other that happened to co-vary with it · outcome: held
span.quote: For this purpose, we designed an in vitro RNA mixture experiment (Fig. 3a). Immune populations were purified from healthy donors’ peripheral blood; their RNAs were extracted and mixed in highly variable concentrations (from 0.7 to 46 % of the sample’s RNA). The RNA proportions of the populations were arranged in two transposed latin squares to avoid collinearity and thus ensure specificity (Additional file 1: Table S10). The mixtures were further diluted in a fixed amount of a solution containing mRNA extracted from HCT-116, a colorectal cancer cell line.

span.label: immunohistochemical digital quantification of three cell densities on tissue sections from 38 colorectal tumours, compared against the corresponding scores
span.note: eliminates: in vitro mixtures standing in for tissue - purified RNA mixed in a tube is not a tumour, and the ex vivo check is on real infiltrate · outcome: held
span.quote: In addition, immunohistochemical (IHC) digital quantification of CD3+, CD8α+, and CD68+ cell densities were performed on tissue sections from 38 colorectal cancer tumors. The IHC-measured density of each cell population was found to correlate with the corresponding MCP-counter score (Fig. 3e).

span.label: a simulation in which the within-leukocyte proportions are held constant and equal while the tumour fraction varies, run through both methods
span.note: eliminates: the two methods being compared on a case that cannot separate them - this one is built so that the correct answers differ, and both give theirs · outcome: held
span.quote: To illustrate these differences, we simulated mRNA mixtures where the within-leukocyte proportion of five immune cell populations was kept constant and equal while the proportions of tumor cells varied (Fig. 4a). In this setting, only MCP-counter was able to accurately reflect the difference in immune cell abundances across simulated mixtures, while CIBERSORT (accurately) estimated stable proportions of each immune cell population within the leukocytic fraction of the simulated mixtures.

span.label: marker sets from two previously published methods scored on the same three microenvironment series as this one
span.note: eliminates: the comparison being against the competitors' published numbers rather than against their markers on identical data · outcome: held
span.quote: Different transcriptome-based computational methods were recently proposed to characterize the proportions of immune populations within leukocytes but omit the critical parameter of the overall abundance of leukocytes in the sample. Other published methods lack quantitative validation or are limited to only two cell populations.

span.label: a limit of detection established per population against non-hematopoietic control samples
span.note: eliminates: a score being read as presence at any level - below the stated fraction the method cannot distinguish the population from a sample containing none · outcome: held
span.quote: Finally, we assessed the limit of detection of the technique for each cell population using non-hematopoietic control samples. For each assayed population, we observed a limit of detection below 2 % (depending on the population, from 1/950 to 1/50 of the sample’s total RNA; Fig. 3b). Altogether, these results validate the use of the MCP-counter method to directly compare the abundance of the corresponding cell population across transcriptomic samples.

span.label: the same tumour analysis repeated on three transcriptomic platforms across more than 19,000 samples
span.note: eliminates: a platform-specific artefact being reported as biology, within the constraint that the units themselves are not comparable across platforms · outcome: partial
span.quote: Nonetheless, we showed that the relative cellular abundance across three large tumor datasets, totaling more than 19,000 tumors and obtained with three different gene expression platforms, are largely consistent (Additional file 2: Figure S10), validating the use of MCP-counter to assess which samples are most or least infiltrated by each characterized cell population.

span.label: the discovery set spanning 344 different culture conditions, purification methods and cell treatments
span.note: eliminates: marker genes selected because of the conditions the reference cells were grown in rather than because of the cell type · outcome: held
span.quote: The 81 datasets from the discovery set spanned 344 different culture conditions, purification methods, and cell treatments, which ensures that the selection of TM was not sensitive to experimental conditions.

span.label: MCP-counter
span.quote: MCP-counter estimates are “single sample” scores, in the sense that they are computed on each sample independently. These scores can then be used for direct comparisons of the abundance of the corresponding cell type across samples within a cohort.

span.label: transcriptomic markers
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: cell population
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: negative controls
span.quote: These transcriptomes were normalized to allow their integration into a large meta-dataset which includes 1194 immune or non-immune microenvironment cell population samples; 742 tumor cell line samples were included as negative controls (Additional file 1: Table S1). No hematopoietic tumor cell line was included as a negative control as the transcriptome of these cells is closely related to that of non-malignant hematopoietic cells.

span.label: arbitrary units
span.quote: MCP-counter scores linearly correlate with the corresponding cell population abundances across samples, but they are expressed in arbitrary units. These arbitrary units are dependent on the gene expression platform used to produce the data and one can only compare samples produced with the same gene expression platforms.

span.label: CIBERSORT
span.quote: MCP-counter differs from methods such as CIBERSORT, which aims to measure intra-sample (within-leukocyte) proportions of immune cell populations, while MCP-counter outputs an abundance estimate per cell population that enables an inter-sample comparison, at the cost of being expressed in arbitrary units.

span.label: flow cytometry
span.quote: It conceptually differs from flow cytometry experiments or flow cytometry-inspired computational methods such as CIBERSORT, which aim at describing the relative proportions of various cell populations within a single sample (Fig. 4a). In contrast, MCP-counter is specifically designed to compare the absolute abundance of a given cell population across multiple samples.

span.label: limit of detection
span.quote: Finally, we assessed the limit of detection of the technique for each cell population using non-hematopoietic control samples. For each assayed population, we observed a limit of detection below 2 % (depending on the population, from 1/950 to 1/50 of the sample’s total RNA; Fig. 3b). Altogether, these results validate the use of the MCP-counter method to directly compare the abundance of the corresponding cell population across transcriptomic samples.

span.label: immunohistochemical
span.quote: In addition, immunohistochemical (IHC) digital quantification of CD3+, CD8α+, and CD68+ cell densities were performed on tissue sections from 38 colorectal cancer tumors. The IHC-measured density of each cell population was found to correlate with the corresponding MCP-counter score (Fig. 3e).

span.label: what an MCP-counter score is - IN THE ABSTRACT: a robust quantification of the ABSOLUTE abundance of ten cell populations
span.quote: We introduce the Microenvironment Cell Populations-counter (MCP-counter) method, which allows the robust quantification of the absolute abundance of eight immune and two stromal cell populations in heterogeneous tissues from transcriptomic data. We present in vitro mRNA mixture and ex vivo immunohistochemical data that quantitatively support the validity of our method’s estimates.

span.label: what an MCP-counter score is - IN THE RESULTS: a measure of the INTER-SAMPLE RELATIVE abundance of one population
span.quote: We designed a method, called MCP-counter, with the objective of measuring the inter-sample relative abundance of different cell populations in a microenvironment. To develop and validate our method, we designed a seven step strategy (Fig. 1).

span.label: what an MCP-counter score is - IN THE DISCUSSION: linearly correlated with abundance, in ARBITRARY UNITS that depend on the gene expression platform, comparable only between samples run on the same platform
span.quote: MCP-counter scores linearly correlate with the corresponding cell population abundances across samples, but they are expressed in arbitrary units. These arbitrary units are dependent on the gene expression platform used to produce the data and one can only compare samples produced with the same gene expression platforms.

span.label: what the score answers - MCP-COUNTER: is there more of this cell type in sample A than in sample B
span.quote: MCP-counter differs from methods such as CIBERSORT, which aims to measure intra-sample (within-leukocyte) proportions of immune cell populations, while MCP-counter outputs an abundance estimate per cell population that enables an inter-sample comparison, at the cost of being expressed in arbitrary units.

span.label: gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within that population - a definition the authors note is restrictive enough that such markers may not exist for a given population
span.quote: MCP-counter is based on the methodological framework of transcriptomic markers (TM), defined as gene expression features expressed in one and only one cell population and whose expression shows little variation within the population of interest (step 1). It directly follows that, within a sample composed of many different cell populations, the abundance of the population of interest is proportional to the sample’s expression of its related TM. Given their restrictive definition, TM are not guaranteed to exist for all populations.

span.label: the scale of an MCP-counter score: linearly correlated with abundance, dependent on the gene expression platform, and comparable only between samples run on the same platform
span.quote: MCP-counter scores linearly correlate with the corresponding cell population abundances across samples, but they are expressed in arbitrary units. These arbitrary units are dependent on the gene expression platform used to produce the data and one can only compare samples produced with the same gene expression platforms.

span.label: the Pearson correlations between scores and known RNA proportions in the in vitro mixtures
span.quote: Transcriptome analyses revealed that MCP-counter scores were highly correlated with the cell proportions for the populations introduced in the mixtures (Fig. 3b), with Pearson’s correlation coefficients ranging from 0.94 to 0.99.

span.label: the AUC floor for every signature across 4804 validation samples
span.quote: MCP-counter scores exhibit a clear separation of the cell types in the discovery and two validation series (Fig. 2b), with an AUC above 0.994 for each signature on the 4804 validation samples

span.label: the upper bound on the limit of detection for every population assayed - from 1/950 to 1/50 of total RNA depending on which
span.quote: Finally, we assessed the limit of detection of the technique for each cell population using non-hematopoietic control samples. For each assayed population, we observed a limit of detection below 2 % (depending on the population, from 1/950 to 1/50 of the sample’s total RNA; Fig. 3b). Altogether, these results validate the use of the MCP-counter method to directly compare the abundance of the corresponding cell population across transcriptomic samples.
